description: Results from the literature that bear on this repository's numbers and verdicts, each read from its primary source. A person adds entries; nothing here is ingested automatically. Every claim names the setting it holds in, one kind of evidence and what it does not establish, so the qualifiers travel with the number. Schema: frontier_results.schema.json. Guard: tooling/test_frontier_results.py. Evidence values: .github/skills/scientific-claims/SKILL.md.

citation.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models

see_also.note: The authors' repository: task definitions, circuits, evaluator, certified counts in each task's results.jsonl, and the Lean 4 proofs. Apache-2.0. Its README repeats the paper's Table I.

claims.statement: In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art.
claims.location: Abstract; per-task counts in Table 1, repeated in the uncompute README
conditions: Each task is one subroutine of a fault-tolerant algorithm, specified as a reversible action on computational-basis states
Logical counts: T is the Toffoli count, with Toffoli and CCZ counted equally, and Q is the peak number of logical qubits
The kickmix circuit model of Babbush et al. (arXiv:2603.28846): classical reversible gates, X-basis measurement-based uncomputation and diagonal phase gates
Circuits are ranked by the TQ-cost, T x Q, which the authors chose for a uniform comparison and say depends on hardware in practice
G_TQ is the baseline TQ-cost divided by the discovered TQ-cost; where a baseline has free parameters they are chosen to minimise its TQ-cost
Candidates were proposed by Claude Mythos 5 inside OpenEvolve and scored by an evaluator the model could not see into
does_not_establish: Execution on quantum hardware
End-to-end algorithm costs: each task is one subroutine

claims.statement: A complete benchmark circuit built on this inversion (SI II) uses 4.0 million Toffolis and 935 qubits.
conditions: Elliptic-curve point addition built on a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion using divsteps. Most branch decisions are recovered from the arithmetic state instead of being stored, and a tunable cutoff decides which are decoded and which are stored

claims.statement: Correctness is checked by sampling: if all k independent tests pass, then with confidence 1 - δ the probability ε of a defective computational-basis trajectory satisfies ε <= 1 - δ^(1/k), approximately ln(1/δ)/k, and the state fidelity is at least (1 - 2ε)^2.

citation.title: Magic state cultivation: growing T states as cheap as CNOT gates

see_also.note: The authors' simulation data. qdk 1.31.0's qdk.qre.models.factories.GSJ24Factory is built on it, for physical error rates 5e-4, 1e-3 and 2e-3. That class's docstring cites this paper under another title and with a wrong initial for the second author; cite the arXiv record.

claims.statement: Compared to prior work, cultivation uses an order of magnitude fewer qubit-rounds to reach logical error rates as low as 2·10^-9 when subjected to 10^-3 uniform depolarizing circuit noise. Halving the circuit noise to 5·10^-4 improves the achievable logical error rate to 4·10^-11.

citation.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits

claims.statement: I estimate that a 2048 bit RSA integer could be factored in less than a week by a quantum computer with less than a million noisy qubits.
conditions: A square grid of qubits with nearest-neighbour connections
A uniform gate error rate of 0.1%
A surface code cycle time of 1 microsecond and a control system reaction time of 10 microseconds
The reduction comes mainly from approximate residue arithmetic, yoked surface codes for idle logical qubits, and allocating less space to magic state distillation by using magic state cultivation
does_not_establish: Execution on quantum hardware
A logical-qubit count: the abstract gives none, so read the body before quoting one

qualifiers: 0.1% uniform gate error, 1 microsecond cycle, 10 microsecond reaction time, square grid
Under the same assumptions
